context: Address each risk where it actually lives rather than restating it in another report. Move the privacy canary out of the evaluated repository or generate it per-run so a tool call cannot reach a committed copy, and add a scenario check that fails when the canary is reachable from the session cwd. Freeze the acceptance criteria and the tracker prose in one versioned contract document per generation so the bar is unambiguous at read time. Extend preflight identity to fail closed when the served model or CLI build differs from the pinned identity of the generation being compared against.
description: Three residual validity risks carried forward from the v2 and v3 packets that were never converted into tracked work. One, the privacy canary string sk-fixture-DO-NOT-ECHO lives in the same repository the evaluation sessions run in (corpus.py, score.py, tests/scorers), and a v2 treatment session reached it through a tool call, so the sensitive-content scenario's arm separation is weak and a privacy pass may reflect co-location rather than restraint. Two, the acceptance methodology drifted mid-effort from total context with a 30 percent Codex reduction target to incremental memory payload; the newer metric is better, but criteria and tracker prose were never frozen together, so a later reader cannot tell which bar a generation was judged against. Three, results are pinned to specific model and CLI builds (gpt-5.6-sol, claude-opus-4-6), and a provider upgrade silently invalidates comparability across generations. Sources reports/promotion-decision.md known evidence caveats and reports/final-completion-plan.md additional risks.
